findings.claim: The observed selection window is the native score-clock interval [0.0, 0.5] with 50 recorded score times at 0.01 spacing; the learning window equals this same interval, so no extrapolation beyond the observed support is licensed.

Recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so the supplied clock observation carries no decoded-affinity label; any coordinate contrast here is selection/score-clock evidence, not measured final benefit.

The coordinate representation is native model endpoint world coordinates, and the incumbent reward view is an endpoint pointcloud with a FLOWR endpoint VJP derivative path; the registered reward-route choices vary only delta_A over the same score times with dose_factors fixed at 1.0.

hypotheses.direction: Contrast between the rising-delta_A schedule and the constant-delta_A control should be non-stationary across the window rather than flat.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the endpoint coordinate contrast between the rising-delta_A schedule and the constant-delta_A control is statistically indistinguishable from a stationary (time-invariant) profile across the whole observed window, the hypothesis is falsified.
hypotheses.observable: Endpoint pointcloud coordinate observables (landmark local dx/dy/dz and soft_mass) evaluated at the recorded score times.
hypotheses.scope: Global over the observed window [0.0, 0.5]; no extrapolation past 0.5.
hypotheses.statement: A time-dependent curvature schedule on the endpoint pointcloud reward (delta_A rising from 0.5 toward 1.0 across the observed window, as in the registered C1 recipe) is associated with a changing contrast in endpoint coordinate observables over the full observed window, relative to the constant-curvature control C2.

hypotheses.direction: Sign of the early-versus-late coordinate contrast should reverse between the rising and falling schedules.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the rising and falling delta_A schedules yield coordinate contrasts of the same sign and comparable magnitude across the window, the timing interpretation is falsified.
hypotheses.observable: Endpoint pointcloud coordinate observables at the recorded score times, compared between the rising and falling delta_A schedules.
hypotheses.statement: The opposite-timing control (delta_A falling from 1.0 toward 0.5, registered C3) should produce a coordinate contrast of opposite sign to the rising schedule at matched dose, isolating timing rather than magnitude of curvature.

limitations: No temporal profiles are available in this packet (temporal_profiles_available=false); the supplied clock observation is metadata only and does not contain per-time coordinate values.

The clock observation reports no decoded affinity labels (recorded affinities removed; equal score prior), so no claim about final predicted target affinity or descendant survival can be supported from this evidence.
The registered recipes are predeclared interventions, not discovered stage boundaries; the knots_origin field explicitly states they are not a discovered biological stage.
No independent batches, confidence intervals, or p-values are present in the delivered clock observation, so statistical support for any coordinate contrast is unquantified here.
The coordinate observables are untyped proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is warranted.
